title: QA Validation Frameworks
summary: Notebook-based, SQL-first validation frameworks for Fabric medallion pipelines: row counts, transformations, schema, freshness and metric reconciliation, with structured results, gates and alerts.
audience: Data engineers, QA analysts, data architects, DevOps engineers

pages.title: Overview
pages.description: What the validation frameworks give you, when to use them, scope, prerequisites and a map of the playbook.

pages.title: Architecture and design principles
pages.description: The three frameworks, the validation type matrix, design principles, workspace layout, data flow and naming rules including four-part names and T-SQL versus Spark SQL.

pages.title: Results model and tolerances
pages.description: The results and run tables, status model, severity, and how to design tolerances, warning bands and expected-reject accounting.

pages.title: Harness and core checks
pages.description: The notebook harness and the row count, transformation, schema and freshness checks with copy-ready code, success criteria and example output.

pages.title: Complex and extended checks
pages.description: Complex metric reconciliation with rolling fiscal windows, plus duplicate, null, referential integrity, drift, layer reconciliation and late-arriving data checks.

pages.title: Orchestration, gating and reporting
pages.description: Running validations from pipelines, gating promotion on results, alerting on failure and reporting results through a semantic model.

pages.title: Governance and troubleshooting
pages.description: Ownership roles, change control, adding a validation, versioning, performance guidance, troubleshooting tables and common pitfalls.

pages.title: Comparison with other tools
pages.description: How the framework compares with Delta constraints, materialized lake view constraints, Purview data quality, Great Expectations, Deequ, Soda and dbt tests, with a decision table and checklist.
